claims.text: Morgan Stanley converts workplace and stock-plan participants into wealth management clients through its client acquisition funnel, in which the Workplace channel is the top of the funnel, and workplace assets migrate over time into the advisor-led channel via referral models, financial education, and advice offerings.

Morgan Stanley describes its three channels—financial advisors, Workplace, and E*TRADE—as together comprising its strategic client acquisition model, with Workplace positioned as the top of the funnel for acquiring wealth management clients.

On the first-quarter 2026 call, the CFO described the funnel as beginning with retaining vested workplace assets (which translates into net new assets), followed over time by channel migration where workplace assets seek advice and move into the adviser-led channel.
Morgan Stanley defines channel migration as workplace assets that began in the Workplace channel moving into the advisor-led channel, with $300 billion doing so since 2020.
The firm attributes the migration of workplace-originated assets into the advisor-led channel to its consistent investments in its differentiated platform.
On the second-quarter 2026 call, management said Workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform, then the firm delivers advice and solutions to build fee-based assets.

Morgan Stanley describes its Morgan Stanley at Work business as positioning it as an early trusted advisor to private companies, where employees benefit from management of equity compensation plans, liquidity opportunities, and full-service advice as companies grow.
The firm describes its investments in the self-directed and Workplace channels as driving its differentiated client acquisition funnel.
Morgan Stanley states that 70% of the flows that originate from workplace are net new assets to the firm.
Since 2020, Morgan Stanley states it has generated over $400 billion of new adviser-led assets from relationships that originated from either Workplace or E*TRADE.
Morgan Stanley describes a referral-based partnership with Carta under which private companies moving from private to public are referred to Morgan Stanley, supporting conversion onto its platform.

The strategic-update deck depicts a client lifecycle in which workplace founders and employees move from financial wellness and equity compensation through to full-service wealth advice and asset allocation as companies go public.
Morgan Stanley defines the workplace channel as including equity compensation solutions for companies, their executives and employees.

The firm defines stock plan participants as total accounts with vested and/or unvested stock plan assets in the workplace channel, with individuals holding accounts in multiple plans counted in each plan.
On the third-quarter 2025 call, the CFO described the workplace channel as a powerful asset acquisition tool, with the reopening of the IPO market supporting net new assets.
On the second-quarter 2026 call, the CFO said Workplace is a strong contributor to the top of the funnel, with stock plan IPO flows representing just over half of overall net new assets that quarter.
The CEO said the financial advisors, Workplace, and E*TRADE channels together comprise the firm's strategic client acquisition model.
Advisor-led assets originating from workplace and E*TRADE relationships grew to a record $99 billion for full-year 2025, versus historical averages of around $60 billion per year.

In the first quarter of 2025, assets migrating to the advisor-led channel that originated from the workplace channel increased by an incremental $20 billion, adding to roughly $300 billion accumulated from workplace since the channel expanded in 2020.

On the second-quarter 2026 call, the firm said it has about 70% of the top 100 unicorns by market cap in its workplace pipeline, with IPOs serving as a source of net new assets at the top of the funnel.
The CFO said 70% of the flows that originate from the workplace channel are actually net new assets to the firm.

On the second-quarter 2026 call, the CFO said the firm is working on a referral model that can begin as early as the financial education spot to convert workplace clients into advice-based (advisor-led) relationships.
The CEO said the Morgan Stanley at Work business positions the firm as an early trusted advisor to over 50,000 private companies.
On the second-quarter 2025 call, the CFO said the firm historically had about $16 billion per year originating from workplace and was running ahead of that in 2025.

On the third-quarter 2025 call, the CFO cited a $300 billion workplace migration figure and about $60 billion of migration per year historically, saying workplace has contributed to net new assets, fee-based flows, and channel migration.
The strategic update deck showed advisor-led flows from workplace and E*TRADE of approximately $60 billion average for 2020-2024 and approximately $100 billion for 2025.

On the third-quarter 2026 call, the CEO described attachment points that bring clients to E*TRADE and, where appropriate, fee-based flows that make their way to advisers, with clients acquired in the corporate stock plan (workplace) context.
The CFO said the firm's pipeline and connectivity across channels allows it to build relationships early and deepen them over time.

Morgan Stanley's Workplace channel includes equity compensation solutions (stock plan administration) for companies, their executives and employees, serving as the entry point through which workplace participants are engaged.

The firm's Wealth Management segment provides workplace services, including stock plan administration, and retirement plan services, as one of three channels (Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace).

The strategic-update deck shows a client lifecycle offering spanning financial wellness and employee benefits, founders wealth strategies, full-service wealth advice and asset allocation, family office solutions, trust and estate planning, private shares trading and lending, and IPO execution and support services.

The firm's MS at Work offering provides stock plan and 401(k) administration, cap table management, cash management solutions, and private capital markets/tender/financing and IPO services for late-stage/IPO companies.

Morgan Stanley uses referral models and technology such as the LeadIQ product to match individuals (including workplace participants) with advisers, with the goal of becoming their principal financial adviser.

Through its exclusive partnership with Carta, private stock plan/corporate companies are referred to Morgan Stanley as they go public, providing a seamless experience to convert those participants into wealth clients.
Morgan Stanley offers advice-based services to founders and individuals of private companies through its Carta relationship, deepening relationships as companies transition from private to public.
The firm's referral model for workplace participants can begin as early as the financial education spot and with 401(k) assets, to help individuals understand where they could use advice.
Morgan Stanley continues to expand its retirement capabilities and deepen engagement with plan participants, creating opportunities to build advice-based relationships over time.
Morgan Stanley provides financial wellness programs to company employees as part of the Integrated Firm, spanning from advice in corporate boardrooms to financial wellness programs for employees.
Morgan Stanley uses an AI-powered lead distribution platform called LeadIQ that matches workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitates engagement with financial advisors.
For workplace participants who do not yet have an advice-based relationship, the firm works a referral model that can begin as early as the financial education spot and through 401(k) assets.
Morgan Stanley drives channel migration from workplace to advisor-led through technology and investment, as workplace assets begin seeking advice.
Assets that originate from workplace migrate into the advisor-led channel as a result of consistent investments into its differentiated platform.

Morgan Stanley at Work, through its exclusive partnership with Carta, positions the firm as an early trusted advisor to private companies, and employees benefit from equity compensation plan management, liquidity opportunities, and full-service advice.
The firm begins at the top of the funnel with corporate coverage, using the Integrated Firm to build corporate relationships that lead to workplace relationships.
Advisors engage retail clients by sending next best actions, and Morgan Stanley has seen increased responses to these engagements.
Morgan Stanley states that since 2020 it has seen $300 billion of assets initiate in the Workplace channel and move into the advisor-led channel.
The firm states it has seen about $60 billion of workplace-to-advisor-led migration per year, and as of the third quarter of 2025 was exceeding that pace on a full-year basis.
The firm defines Advisor-Led Flows from Workplace and E*TRADE as assets brought into advisor-led relationships where the initial account was workplace or self-directed.

As of the third quarter of 2025, Morgan Stanley reports LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships, as one of its early AI use cases, some live and some in pilot.

As of the fourth quarter of 2024, the firm reports a recently announced partnership with Carta that puts it at the center of new client stock plan opportunities as private companies consider going public.

As of the third quarter of 2025, Morgan Stanley reports deepening its competitive moats through an expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets and announced partnerships with Zero Hash in digital assets.

As of the fourth quarter of 2025, the firm reports that its Morgan Stanley at Work business, through its exclusive partnership with Carta, positions it as an early trusted advisor to over 50,000 private companies.

Morgan Stanley positions its workplace and stock-plan conversion efforts as industry-leading and differentiated—claiming a singular position in the industry from its integrated client acquisition funnel, about 70% of the top 100 unicorns in its workplace pipeline, and industry-leading net new assets—but these are the firm's own self-positioning statements rather than independently measured competitor data, so an objective cross-firm comparison cannot be made on this evidence.
